messages.subject: Re: Why does system() seem to cause Shiny to block even when wait=FALSE?
parts:
If intern=TRUE, then wait=FALSE is ignored. Which makes sense if you think about it :)
On Sat, Nov 26, 2016 at 11:08 AM Bryan Britten <britte...@gmail.com> wrote:
This question was also asked on Stack Overflow, so please excuse the redundancy if you've seen it in both places.

I'm building a Shiny app that makes a call to Python in order to parse large files, but it appears that when R makes a call to system, this prevents the whole app from moving forward. In addition, if one user has already created a session and all inputs/outputs are loaded, but then invokes the system call, future users cannot launch the app. My assumption was that by creating objects from the system call, using wait=FALSE, and employing req(future_object, cancelOutput=FALSE) in my outputs would allow the app to continue chugging along.


However, it doesn't seem like that's the case. Below is a MRE where the system call is outside of the ui and server assignments, which causes the whole app to wait until the system call has finished. If I move it inside of the server portion of the app, the title of the app will show up, but the datatable output won't appear until the system call is done.


My question is why does Shiny shut down when a system call is made, even if wait is set to FALSE? 


library(shiny)
library(ggplot2) # for mpg dataset

x = {system("python ~/Playground/Syntax/py_test.py", intern=TRUE, wait=FALSE)}
ui = fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Testing Non-Blocking"),

  fluidRow(
    DT::dataTableOutput("table")
  ),
  fluidRow(
    textOutput("text")
  )
)

server = function(input, output, session) {

  output$table <- DT::renderDataTable(DT::datatable({
    data <- mpg
    data
  }))

  output$text <- renderText({
    req(x, cancelOutput=FALSE)
    x
  })

}

shinyApp(ui=ui, server=server)


PYTHON CODE

import time

def main():
  print "Hello, World!"
  time.sleep(10)
  print "I think I'll stop running now"

if __name__ == "__main__":
  main()
